work.title: The Third Part of King Henry the Sixth
work.author: William Shakespeare

content.text: Alarum. Enter Richard, Duke of York.

lines.text: The army of the Queen hath got the field.
lines.plainText: The army of the Queen hath got the field

lines.text: My uncles both are slain in rescuing me;
lines.plainText: My uncles both are slain in rescuing me

lines.text: And all my followers to the eager foe
lines.plainText: And all my followers to the eager foe

lines.text: Turn back and fly like ships before the wind,
lines.plainText: Turn back and fly like ships before the wind

lines.text: Or lambs pursued by hunger-starved wolves.
lines.plainText: Or lambs pursued by hungerstarved wolves

lines.text: My sons, God knows what hath bechanced them;
lines.plainText: My sons God knows what hath bechanced them

lines.text: But this I know, they have demeaned themselves
lines.plainText: But this I know they have demeaned themselves

lines.text: Like men born to renown by life or death.
lines.plainText: Like men born to renown by life or death

lines.text: Three times did Richard make a lane to me,
lines.plainText: Three times did Richard make a lane to me

lines.text: And thrice cried "Courage, father, fight it out!"
lines.plainText: And thrice cried Courage father fight it out

lines.text: And full as oft came Edward to my side
lines.plainText: And full as oft came Edward to my side

lines.text: With purple falchion painted to the hilt
lines.plainText: With purple falchion painted to the hilt

lines.text: In blood of those that had encountered him;
lines.plainText: In blood of those that had encountered him

lines.text: And when the hardiest warriors did retire,
lines.plainText: And when the hardiest warriors did retire

lines.text: Richard cried "Charge, and give no foot of ground!"
lines.plainText: Richard cried Charge and give no foot of ground

lines.text: And cried "A crown, or else a glorious tomb!
lines.plainText: And cried A crown or else a glorious tomb

lines.text: A sceptre, or an earthly sepulchre!"
lines.plainText: A sceptre or an earthly sepulchre

lines.text: With this we charged again; but, out, alas!
lines.plainText: With this we charged again but out alas

lines.text: We budged again, as I have seen a swan
lines.plainText: We budged again as I have seen a swan

lines.text: With bootless labour swim against the tide
lines.plainText: With bootless labour swim against the tide

lines.text: And spend her strength with over-matching waves.
lines.plainText: And spend her strength with overmatching waves

content.text: Enter Queen Margaret, Clifford, Northumberland, the young Prince Edward and Soldiers.

lines.text: Yield to our mercy, proud Plantagenet.
lines.plainText: Yield to our mercy proud Plantagenet

lines.text: Ay, to such mercy as his ruthless arm
lines.plainText: Ay to such mercy as his ruthless arm

lines.text: With downright payment showed unto my father.
lines.plainText: With downright payment showed unto my father

lines.text: Now Phaëthon hath tumbled from his car,
lines.plainText: Now Phathon hath tumbled from his car

lines.text: And made an evening at the noontide prick.
lines.plainText: And made an evening at the noontide prick

lines.text: My ashes, as the phoenix, may bring forth
lines.plainText: My ashes as the phoenix may bring forth

lines.text: A bird that will revenge upon you all;
lines.plainText: A bird that will revenge upon you all

lines.text: And in that hope I throw mine eyes to heaven,
lines.plainText: And in that hope I throw mine eyes to heaven

lines.text: Scorning whate'er you can afflict me with.
lines.plainText: Scorning whate'er you can afflict me with

lines.text: Why come you not? What, multitudes, and fear?
lines.plainText: Why come you not What multitudes and fear

lines.text: So cowards fight when they can fly no further;
lines.plainText: So cowards fight when they can fly no further

lines.text: So doves do peck the falcon's piercing talons;
lines.plainText: So doves do peck the falcon's piercing talons

lines.text: So desperate thieves, all hopeless of their lives,
lines.plainText: So desperate thieves all hopeless of their lives

lines.text: Breathe out invectives 'gainst the officers.
lines.plainText: Breathe out invectives 'gainst the officers

lines.text: O Clifford, but bethink thee once again,
lines.plainText: O Clifford but bethink thee once again

lines.text: And in thy thought o'errun my former time;
lines.plainText: And in thy thought o'errun my former time

lines.text: And, if thou canst for blushing, view this face,
lines.plainText: And if thou canst for blushing view this face

lines.text: And bite thy tongue, that slanders him with cowardice
lines.plainText: And bite thy tongue that slanders him with cowardice

lines.text: Whose frown hath made thee faint and fly ere this.
lines.plainText: Whose frown hath made thee faint and fly ere this

lines.text: I will not bandy with thee word for word,
lines.plainText: I will not bandy with thee word for word

lines.text: But buckle with thee blows twice two for one.
lines.plainText: But buckle with thee blows twice two for one

lines.text: Hold, valiant Clifford; for a thousand causes
lines.plainText: Hold valiant Clifford for a thousand causes

lines.text: I would prolong awhile the traitor's life.
lines.plainText: I would prolong awhile the traitor's life

lines.text: Wrath makes him deaf; speak thou, Northumberland.
lines.plainText: Wrath makes him deaf speak thou Northumberland

lines.text: Hold, Clifford, do not honour him so much
lines.plainText: Hold Clifford do not honour him so much

lines.text: To prick thy finger, though to wound his heart.
lines.plainText: To prick thy finger though to wound his heart

lines.text: What valour were it, when a cur doth grin,
lines.plainText: What valour were it when a cur doth grin

lines.text: For one to thrust his hand between his teeth,
lines.plainText: For one to thrust his hand between his teeth

lines.text: When he might spurn him with his foot away?
lines.plainText: When he might spurn him with his foot away

lines.text: It is war's prize to take all vantages,
lines.plainText: It is war's prize to take all vantages

lines.text: And ten to one is no impeach of valour.
lines.plainText: And ten to one is no impeach of valour

content.text: [They lay hands on York, who struggles.]

lines.text: Ay, ay, so strives the woodcock with the gin.
lines.plainText: Ay ay so strives the woodcock with the gin

lines.text: So doth the cony struggle in the net.
lines.plainText: So doth the cony struggle in the net

lines.text: So triumph thieves upon their conquered booty;
lines.plainText: So triumph thieves upon their conquered booty

lines.text: So true men yield, with robbers so o'ermatched.
lines.plainText: So true men yield with robbers so o'ermatched

lines.text: What would your Grace have done unto him now?
lines.plainText: What would your Grace have done unto him now

lines.text: Brave warriors, Clifford and Northumberland,
lines.plainText: Brave warriors Clifford and Northumberland

lines.text: Come, make him stand upon this molehill here,
lines.plainText: Come make him stand upon this molehill here

lines.text: That raught at mountains with outstretched arms,
lines.plainText: That raught at mountains with outstretched arms

lines.text: Yet parted but the shadow with his hand.
lines.plainText: Yet parted but the shadow with his hand

lines.text: What, was it you that would be England's king?
lines.plainText: What was it you that would be England's king

lines.text: Was 't you that revelled in our parliament
lines.plainText: Was 't you that revelled in our parliament

lines.text: And made a preachment of your high descent?
lines.plainText: And made a preachment of your high descent

lines.text: Where are your mess of sons to back you now,
lines.plainText: Where are your mess of sons to back you now

lines.text: The wanton Edward and the lusty George?
lines.plainText: The wanton Edward and the lusty George

lines.text: And where's that valiant crook-back prodigy,
lines.plainText: And where's that valiant crookback prodigy

lines.text: Dicky your boy, that with his grumbling voice
lines.plainText: Dicky your boy that with his grumbling voice

lines.text: Was wont to cheer his dad in mutinies?
lines.plainText: Was wont to cheer his dad in mutinies

lines.text: Or, with the rest, where is your darling Rutland?
lines.plainText: Or with the rest where is your darling Rutland

lines.text: Look, York, I stained this napkin with the blood
lines.plainText: Look York I stained this napkin with the blood

lines.text: That valiant Clifford with his rapier's point
lines.plainText: That valiant Clifford with his rapier's point

lines.text: Made issue from the bosom of the boy;
lines.plainText: Made issue from the bosom of the boy

lines.text: And if thine eyes can water for his death,
lines.plainText: And if thine eyes can water for his death

lines.text: I give thee this to dry thy cheeks withal.
lines.plainText: I give thee this to dry thy cheeks withal

lines.text: Alas, poor York, but that I hate thee deadly
lines.plainText: Alas poor York but that I hate thee deadly

lines.text: I should lament thy miserable state.
lines.plainText: I should lament thy miserable state

lines.text: I prithee grieve to make me merry, York;
lines.plainText: I prithee grieve to make me merry York

lines.text: Stamp, rave, and fret, that I may sing and dance.
lines.plainText: Stamp rave and fret that I may sing and dance

lines.text: What, hath thy fiery heart so parched thine entrails
lines.plainText: What hath thy fiery heart so parched thine entrails

lines.text: That not a tear can fall for Rutland's death?
lines.plainText: That not a tear can fall for Rutland's death

lines.text: Why art thou patient, man? Thou shouldst be mad;
lines.plainText: Why art thou patient man Thou shouldst be mad

lines.text: And I, to make thee mad, do mock thee thus.
lines.plainText: And I to make thee mad do mock thee thus

lines.text: Stamp, rave, and fret, that I may sing and dance.
lines.plainText: Stamp rave and fret that I may sing and dance

lines.text: Thou would'st be fee'd, I see, to make me sport;
lines.plainText: Thou would'st be fee'd I see to make me sport

lines.text: York cannot speak unless he wear a crown.
lines.plainText: York cannot speak unless he wear a crown

lines.text: A crown for York! And, lords, bow low to him.
lines.plainText: A crown for York And lords bow low to him

lines.text: Hold you his hands whilst I do set it on.
lines.plainText: Hold you his hands whilst I do set it on

content.text: [Putting a paper crown on his head.]

lines.text: That is my office, for my father's sake.
lines.plainText: That is my office for my father's sake

lines.text: Nay, stay; let's hear the orisons he makes.
lines.plainText: Nay stay let's hear the orisons he makes

lines.text: She-wolf of France, but worse than wolves of France,
lines.plainText: Shewolf of France but worse than wolves of France

lines.text: Whose tongue more poisons than the adder's tooth!
lines.plainText: Whose tongue more poisons than the adder's tooth

lines.text: How ill-beseeming is it in thy sex
lines.plainText: How illbeseeming is it in thy sex

lines.text: To triumph like an Amazonian trull
lines.plainText: To triumph like an Amazonian trull

lines.text: Upon their woes whom Fortune captivates!
lines.plainText: Upon their woes whom Fortune captivates

lines.text: But that thy face is vizard-like, unchanging,
lines.plainText: But that thy face is vizardlike unchanging

lines.text: Made impudent with use of evil deeds,
lines.plainText: Made impudent with use of evil deeds

lines.text: I would assay, proud queen, to make thee blush.
lines.plainText: I would assay proud queen to make thee blush

lines.text: To tell thee whence thou cam'st, of whom derived,
lines.plainText: To tell thee whence thou cam'st of whom derived

lines.text: Were shame enough to shame thee, wert thou not shameless.
lines.plainText: Were shame enough to shame thee wert thou not shameless

lines.text: Thy father bears the type of King of Naples,
lines.plainText: Thy father bears the type of King of Naples

lines.text: Of both the Sicils, and Jerusalem,
lines.plainText: Of both the Sicils and Jerusalem

lines.text: Yet not so wealthy as an English yeoman.
lines.plainText: Yet not so wealthy as an English yeoman

lines.text: Hath that poor monarch taught thee to insult?
lines.plainText: Hath that poor monarch taught thee to insult

lines.text: It needs not, nor it boots thee not, proud queen;
lines.plainText: It needs not nor it boots thee not proud queen

lines.text: Unless the adage must be verified,
lines.plainText: Unless the adage must be verified

lines.text: That beggars mounted run their horse to death.
lines.plainText: That beggars mounted run their horse to death

lines.text: 'Tis beauty that doth oft make women proud;
lines.plainText: 'Tis beauty that doth oft make women proud

lines.text: But God he knows thy share thereof is small.
lines.plainText: But God he knows thy share thereof is small

lines.text: 'Tis virtue that doth make them most admired;
lines.plainText: 'Tis virtue that doth make them most admired

lines.text: The contrary doth make thee wondered at.
lines.plainText: The contrary doth make thee wondered at

lines.text: 'Tis government that makes them seem divine;
lines.plainText: 'Tis government that makes them seem divine

lines.text: The want thereof makes thee abominable.
lines.plainText: The want thereof makes thee abominable

lines.text: Thou art as opposite to every good
lines.plainText: Thou art as opposite to every good

lines.text: As the Antipodes are unto us,
lines.plainText: As the Antipodes are unto us

lines.text: Or as the south to the Septentrion.
lines.plainText: Or as the south to the Septentrion

lines.text: O tiger's heart wrapped in a woman's hide!
lines.plainText: O tiger's heart wrapped in a woman's hide

lines.text: How couldst thou drain the life-blood of the child,
lines.plainText: How couldst thou drain the lifeblood of the child

lines.text: To bid the father wipe his eyes withal,
lines.plainText: To bid the father wipe his eyes withal

lines.text: And yet be seen to bear a woman's face?
lines.plainText: And yet be seen to bear a woman's face

lines.text: Women are soft, mild, pitiful, and flexible;
lines.plainText: Women are soft mild pitiful and flexible

lines.text: Thou stern, obdurate, flinty, rough, remorseless.
lines.plainText: Thou stern obdurate flinty rough remorseless

lines.text: Bid'st thou me rage? Why, now thou hast thy wish:
lines.plainText: Bid'st thou me rage Why now thou hast thy wish

lines.text: Wouldst have me weep? Why, now thou hast thy will;
lines.plainText: Wouldst have me weep Why now thou hast thy will

lines.text: For raging wind blows up incessant showers,
lines.plainText: For raging wind blows up incessant showers

lines.text: And when the rage allays, the rain begins.
lines.plainText: And when the rage allays the rain begins

lines.text: These tears are my sweet Rutland's obsequies,
lines.plainText: These tears are my sweet Rutland's obsequies

lines.text: And every drop cries vengeance for his death
lines.plainText: And every drop cries vengeance for his death

lines.text: 'Gainst thee, fell Clifford, and thee, false Frenchwoman.
lines.plainText: 'Gainst thee fell Clifford and thee false Frenchwoman

lines.text: Beshrew me, but his passion moves me so
lines.plainText: Beshrew me but his passion moves me so

lines.text: That hardly can I check my eyes from tears.
lines.plainText: That hardly can I check my eyes from tears

lines.text: That face of his the hungry cannibals
lines.plainText: That face of his the hungry cannibals

lines.text: Would not have touched, would not have stained with blood;
lines.plainText: Would not have touched would not have stained with blood

lines.text: But you are more inhuman, more inexorable,
lines.plainText: But you are more inhuman more inexorable

lines.text: O, ten times more than tigers of Hyrcania.
lines.plainText: O ten times more than tigers of Hyrcania

lines.text: See, ruthless queen, a hapless father's tears.
lines.plainText: See ruthless queen a hapless father's tears

lines.text: This cloth thou dipped'st in blood of my sweet boy,
lines.plainText: This cloth thou dipped'st in blood of my sweet boy

lines.text: And I with tears do wash the blood away.
lines.plainText: And I with tears do wash the blood away

lines.text: Keep thou the napkin, and go boast of this;
lines.plainText: Keep thou the napkin and go boast of this

lines.text: And if thou tell'st the heavy story right,
lines.plainText: And if thou tell'st the heavy story right

lines.text: Upon my soul, the hearers will shed tears;
lines.plainText: Upon my soul the hearers will shed tears

lines.text: Yea, even my foes will shed fast-falling tears
lines.plainText: Yea even my foes will shed fastfalling tears

lines.text: And say "Alas, it was a piteous deed."
lines.plainText: And say Alas it was a piteous deed

lines.text: There, take the crown, and with the crown my curse;
lines.plainText: There take the crown and with the crown my curse

lines.text: And in thy need such comfort come to thee
lines.plainText: And in thy need such comfort come to thee

lines.text: As now I reap at thy too cruel hand!
lines.plainText: As now I reap at thy too cruel hand

lines.text: Hard-hearted Clifford, take me from the world,
lines.plainText: Hardhearted Clifford take me from the world

lines.text: My soul to heaven, my blood upon your heads!
lines.plainText: My soul to heaven my blood upon your heads

lines.text: Had he been slaughter-man to all my kin,
lines.plainText: Had he been slaughterman to all my kin

lines.text: I should not for my life but weep with him,
lines.plainText: I should not for my life but weep with him

lines.text: To see how inly sorrow gripes his soul.
lines.plainText: To see how inly sorrow gripes his soul

lines.text: What, weeping-ripe, my Lord Northumberland?
lines.plainText: What weepingripe my Lord Northumberland

lines.text: Think but upon the wrong he did us all,
lines.plainText: Think but upon the wrong he did us all

lines.text: And that will quickly dry thy melting tears.
lines.plainText: And that will quickly dry thy melting tears

lines.text: Here's for my oath, here's for my father's death.
lines.plainText: Here's for my oath here's for my father's death

lines.text: And here's to right our gentle-hearted king.
lines.plainText: And here's to right our gentlehearted king

lines.text: Open thy gate of mercy, gracious God!
lines.plainText: Open thy gate of mercy gracious God

lines.text: My soul flies through these wounds to seek out Thee.
lines.plainText: My soul flies through these wounds to seek out Thee

lines.text: Off with his head, and set it on York gates;
lines.plainText: Off with his head and set it on York gates

lines.text: So York may overlook the town of York.
lines.plainText: So York may overlook the town of York
